report.headline: The OCEAN(a) outcomes trial of olpasiran cannot be forecast because the trial has not yet read out; event count and on-treatment Lp(a) reduction at the phase 3 dose are unknown.
report.summary: The phase 3 OCEAN(a) trial randomized 7,297 patients with established ASCVD and Lp(a) ≥200 nmol/L to olpasiran or placebo, with a primary endpoint of time to CHD death, myocardial infarction, or urgent coronary revascularization over a median 5-year follow-up (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05581303). Phase 2 data show deep but waning Lp(a) reduction: -97.4% at week 36 (75 mg Q12W) declining to -27.9% at 96 weeks off treatment (Small Interfering RNA to Reduce Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease; The Off-Treatment Effects of Olpasiran on Lipoprotein(a) Lowering: OCEAN(a)-DOSE Extension Period Results). The calculator projects HR 0.772 (22.8% RRR) using the week-36 nadir, requiring 470 events for 80% power, but the sustained effect over 5 years may be far lower. Human genetics strongly support Lp(a) causality (LPA score 0.922, Mendelian randomization ORs 1.38–3.67 per allele) (opentargets:LPA; Genetic variants associated with Lp(a) lipoprotein level and coronary disease). Confidence is medium because the forecast hinges on missing data rather than a demonstrated small effect.
key_evidence: Primary endpoint: time to CHD death, MI, or urgent coronary revascularization; median follow-up 5 years (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05581303)

Phase 2 Lp(a) reduction: -97.4% at week 36 (75 mg Q12W), waning to -27.9% at 96 weeks (Small Interfering RNA to Reduce Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease; The Off-Treatment Effects of Olpasiran on Lipoprotein(a) Lowering: OCEAN(a)-DOSE Extension Period Results)

Phase 2 baseline median Lp(a): 260.3 nmol/L (Small Interfering RNA to Reduce Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease; Olpasiran, Oxidized Phospholipids, and Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers: Results From the OCEAN(a)-DOSE Trial)
Genetic evidence: LPA association score 0.922; MR ORs 1.38–3.67 for coronary disease (opentargets:LPA; Genetic variants associated with Lp(a) lipoprotein level and coronary disease)
Calculator projection: expected HR 0.772 (22.8% RRR); 470 events needed for 80% power (calculator)
report.what_would_change_this: Phase 3 readout with observed HR, confidence interval, total events, and on-treatment Lp(a) reduction trajectory at the actual dose used.
report.readthrough_note: Other Lp(a)-lowering programs in phase 3 include pelacarsen (antisense, HORIZON trial) and lepodisiran (siRNA, Lp(a)HORIZON); their readouts will inform whether sustained Lp(a) reduction translates to cardiovascular benefit in secondary prevention.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: LPA has Open Targets genetic association score 0.922 with coronary artery disease (183 evidence items, 8 before cutoff per f_bbddc6c5c50370), with multiple large-scale GWAS published before cutoff: GCST010479 (n=392,241, 2020-05-29), FINNGEN_R12_I9_UAP (n=460,589), GCST90436075 (n=397,126, 2018-08-13), GCST008370 (n=408,458, 2018-08-13), GCST90013864 (n=352,063, 2021-05-20). Score well above 0.5 threshold with coronary disease studies confirms causal role.
mechanism.notes: Phase 3 dose for NCT05581303 not confirmed in verified facts; used phase 2 OCEAN(a)-DOSE data at 75 mg Q12W (week 36, placebo-adjusted -97.4%, f_8d84d4809e8094) as best available estimate per guidelines. Phase 2 baseline Lp(a) 260.3 nmol/L (f_a8ab77d6d6e252, f_b2009fc9a9094, pmid:36342163, pmid:39937508) converted to mg/dL using standard 2.4 nmol/L = 1 mg/dL yielding 108.5 mg/dL. Outcome trial entry threshold is 200 nmol/L (83.3 mg/dL, f_deaf89093e4158, ctgov:NCT05581303). Effect wanes over time in phase 2: week 60 -76.2% (f_8f280782644c42), week 72 -53.0% (f_8f049f03cf46be), week 84 -44.0% (f_7a3285f171f2ca), week 96 -27.9% (f_46b0c66e023873). No phase 3 biomarker data available. Planned events not reported in verified facts. Median follow-up 5 years per CT.gov (f_cccc70c0ad3b8c). Primary endpoint: time to CHD death, MI, or urgent coronary revascularization (f_74b22224d68598). 7,297 participants randomized (f_227a384ed5a465).

for.text: Calculator outcome is 'not_computable' because the trial has not yet read out; events are unknown (events: null).
Phase 3 enrollment is complete (7,297 randomized) but median follow-up of 5 years is still ongoing per registry.

hypotheses.would_settle: Trial readout with total events and observed HR.

for.text: Phase 2 Lp(a) reduction wanes substantially over time: -97.4% at week 36, -76.2% at 60 weeks, -53.0% at 72 weeks, -44.0% at 84 weeks, -27.9% at 96 weeks (75 mg Q12W). Sustained reduction over 5 years may be far lower than the week-36 value used in the calculator.
Calculator uses week-36 placebo-adjusted reduction (-97.4%) to project a 22.8% RRR (HR 0.772); if sustained reduction is closer to the 96-week value (-27.9%), expected RRR would be much smaller.

against.text: Genetic calibration: LPA variants lowering Lp(a) by ~1 mmol/L LDL-C equivalent associate with ~22% lower CAD risk per year of exposure; the calculator's expected HR 0.772 over 5 years is consistent with this magnitude.
Phase 3 enrollment (7,297) and 5-year follow-up are sized to detect the projected effect; events needed for 80% power is 470.
Phase 2 data show sustained OxPL-apoB reduction (-89.7% at week 36, 75 mg Q12W) without inflammatory signal, suggesting persistent biological effect.

hypotheses.would_settle: Long-term Lp(a) kinetics at the phase 3 dose; trial readout with observed HR.

against.text: LPA genetic association score 0.922 (very high) with coronary artery disease based on 183 studies (8 before cutoff).
Multiple Mendelian randomization studies show Lp(a)-lowering variants causally reduce CAD risk (ORs 1.38–3.67 per allele for increased Lp(a)).
Lp(a) is the intended biomarker; human genetics confirm Lp(a) itself is causal for CAD and aortic-valve calcification.
Phase 1: no serious or fatal adverse events.
Phase 2: injection-site reactions (primarily pain) only; no other safety signals reported.
Olpasiran reduced OxPL-apoB (-89.7% at 75 mg Q12W) without significant effects on hs-CRP or IL-6, indicating no pro-inflammatory off-target effect.
No cardiovascular harm signal in phase 2.

for.text: Phase 3 enrolls patients with established ASCVD and Lp(a) ≥200 nmol/L; phase 2 enrolled ≥150 nmol/L with median baseline 260.3 nmol/L.
In established ASCVD, a substantial fraction of events may be driven by non-Lp(a) pathways (residual LDL, inflammation, thrombosis), potentially diluting the relative benefit of Lp(a) lowering alone.

against.text: Primary endpoint (CHD death, MI, urgent coronary revascularization) is enriched for events on the Lp(a) causal pathway.
Higher Lp(a) threshold (≥200 nmol/L) selects patients more likely to derive benefit from Lp(a) lowering.

Median follow-up of 5 years is adequate for an LDL-C–like cumulative exposure effect.
No active comparator or crossover design reported that would dilute the treatment effect.

issues.issue: Phase 3 dose for NCT05581303 is not confirmed in verified facts. Calculator uses phase 2 week-36 placebo-adjusted Lp(a) reduction at 75 mg Q12W (-97.4%), but no verified fact explicitly states that 75 mg Q12W is the dose selected for the outcomes trial. Per guidelines, this is an acceptable input with a medium-severity caveat (missing phase 3 biomarker data), not a reason to null the input.
issues.request: Add explicit caveat to case narrative and calculator assumptions noting that phase 3 dose is not verified; the phase 2 75 mg Q12W data is used as the closest available proxy.

issues.issue: Automatic check flags 'cites unknown or unverified fact f_b2009fc9a9094' but this fact (pmid:39937508, baseline 260.3 nmol/L) is not referenced in the hypotheses or calculator inputs. The calculator cites pmid:36342163 for the biomarker change. This appears to be a false positive; verify no hidden reference exists.
issues.request: Confirm that f_b2009fc9a9094 is not actually cited anywhere in the case; if it is a false positive, no action needed.

issues.issue: Baseline conversion from 260.3 nmol/L to 108.5 mg/dL uses 2.4 nmol/L = 1 mg/dL factor. This conversion is standard but not explicitly verified in the provided facts. The calculator input should document the conversion factor used.
issues.request: Document the nmol/L to mg/dL conversion factor (2.4) in calculator assumptions or method field for traceability.

issues.issue: Population hypothesis 'for' point claims 'substantial fraction of events may be driven by non-Lp(a) pathways' referencing f_74b22224d68598 (primary endpoint definition). The primary endpoint fact does not directly support this mechanistic claim; it is an inference. Consider weakening the reference or rephrasing.
issues.request: Rephrase population hypothesis to make clear this is an interpretive inference, not a direct fact from the primary endpoint definition, or cite a more appropriate source if available.

issues.issue: Effect_too_small 'against' point cites f_e827313ada0be7 (OxPL-apoB -89.7% at week 36) and f_09b79a45f72ddf ('sustained reduction in OxPL-apoB') to suggest persistent biological effect. The week-36 OxPL-apoB reduction alone does not demonstrate 5-year sustainability; the 'sustained' claim rests on f_09b79a45f72ddf's wording. This is reasonable but should be noted as extrapolation.
issues.request: Clarify in hypothesis that OxPL-apoB sustainability is based on the readout statement's characterization, not direct long-term measurements.
